Cloudflare Workers AI runs the language model. The free plan gives 10,000 \"Neurons\" a day, enough for hundreds of requests, and needs no credit card. If you already have an account, go on.
In the Cloudflare dashboard open AI → Workers AI and choose \"Use REST API\". The Account ID is shown at the top: 32 letters and digits. Copy it and paste it here.
On the same page tap \"Create a Workers AI API Token\", keep the permissions it proposes (Workers AI: Read and Edit) and confirm. Copy the token that appears: Cloudflare shows it only once.
A test request is sent to Cloudflare. The keys stay on this device and in the backups you export.

Optional. The app uses the same account and data as the web version installed on your home server (CasaOS): rooms, groups, custom devices, remotes, schedules and automations are the same everywhere, and the server carries out timers, schedules, automations and alerts on its own, even with the phone off. Without a connection your changes wait on the phone and are sent when the server is back; on a conflict the last change to arrive wins.
The address the installation printed, such as https://casaos.tail1234.ts.net, and your account on the server.
Off: everything stays on this phone

Without https the password and the data travel in clear: only on your home network or behind a proxy with HTTPS.
Which data do you want to use?

Both this phone and the server account may have rooms, groups, custom devices, schedules and automations. With those of the phone they replace the ones of the account, and the Amazon sign-in of the phone goes to the server if it has none. What the phone has now is saved aside: you can go back to it when you disconnect.
The app now uses the home server

The phone goes back to doing everything by itself: timers, schedules, automations and alerts included. Keep the data you have now, those of the server, or go back to those you had before connecting it.

Change the keys of Google Cloud
Six steps, once: about ten minutes. Google Cloud is free and wants no card. Open the links from a computer if it is easier.
Sign in to Google Cloud with your Google account and create a project called Hommaterial.
Check at the top that the project is Hommaterial and tap Enable.
Tap Get started: Hommaterial as name, your email for support and as contact, External as audience. In Branding leave the logo and the domains empty.

In Audience tap Publish app and confirm: the access will not expire. If the button is grey, tap Add users under Test users and add your email: it works at once, but the access has to be linked again every 7 days.
In Clients tap Create client, choose Desktop app as type and tap Create. Copy here the Client ID and the Client secret.

At the end a page opens that does not load, its address starting with http://localhost: copy the whole address and paste it here. If Google says “Error 403: access_denied”, go back to step 4.
